nodes.label: MSc Thesis: Unsupervised Depth Estimation Using Intrinsic Calibration Parameters as Input
nodes.author: Mohammad Amin Ghasemzadeh (advisor: Dr. Behrooz Nasihatkon, K. N. Toosi University of Technology)
nodes.norm_label: msc thesis: unsupervised depth estimation using intrinsic calibration parameters as input

nodes.label: Scale Ambiguity
nodes.rationale: A small near object and a large far object can produce identical sensor images; without camera parameter information the system cannot recover true physical scale, motivating explicit intrinsics input.

nodes.label: Camera Intrinsic Matrix (K)
nodes.rationale: K = [[fx,0,cx],[0,fy,cy],[0,0,1]] encodes focal lengths and principal point; it models the 3D-to-2D projection and its parameters depend on lens focal length, sensor size and image resolution.

nodes.label: Teacher-Student Knowledge Distillation
nodes.rationale: The teacher model transfers structural knowledge and visual features to the student so the student learns physical (metric) scale while preserving structural accuracy.

nodes.label: Depth Anything V2 Base Architecture
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the base model because it is trained via distillation and has strong ability to extract semantic and geometric image features; fine-tuning adds metric depth capability and camera-information adaptation.

nodes.label: DINOv2 Frozen Backbone
nodes.rationale: DINOv2 encoder is frozen during training to preserve training stability and prevent overfitting, based on the assumption that its pre-learned features are already rich enough to represent image content.

nodes.label: Proposed Intrinsics-Conditioned Depth Model
nodes.rationale: The normalized camera intrinsic matrix K is mapped by a fully-connected network into latent space and injected into the decoder as a geometric condition, deliberately separating visual information (encoder) from geometric information (K branch) to reduce sensitivity to calibration changes and increase metric consistency.

nodes.label: Insufficiency of Implicit Camera Handling
nodes.rationale: Models that omit explicit K rely on implicit pixel relations, creating a hidden dependency on the training-set camera distribution; when faced with images from cameras with different parameters they can no longer produce accurate metric estimates, which degrades reliability in heterogeneous real-world deployments.

nodes.label: RMSE Sensitivity to Camera Parameters
nodes.rationale: RMSE depends on absolute depth values, so it reacts directly to geometric camera changes; this apparent limitation is exploited as a diagnostic tool for revealing metric instability of depth models.
